agent_instructions: Interpretation guide: This file contains vanilla Terran ship-part layout data extracted from Cosmoteer rules files under Data/ships/terran. Each part entry includes resolved top-level inherited fields from its Part inheritance chain, but it is not a full semantic execution of the Cosmoteer rules language. price_resources is the build cost from the part Resources block, not a separate market-credit price table. geometry.size is the base-orientation rectangular tile footprint as [width,height]. geometry.footprint_tiles is every tile in that rectangle, using local tile coordinates with origin at the part's top-left tile. travel.blocked_travel_cells is copied from BlockedTravelCells and marks tiles in the footprint that are not traversable for crew pathing. travel.unblocked_footprint_tiles is computed as footprint_tiles minus blocked_travel_cells; use this as the default walkable tile set, but still consider crew_speed_factor, crew_congested_speed_factor, and cell_occupancy_factor when reasoning about movement. doors.allowed_locations uses the game's local part coordinate system and may include coordinates just outside the footprint, because doors are mounted on part edges. geometry.polygon_vertices comes from a PolygonCollider when present and is expressed in local part space rather than tile-center coordinates. geometry.per_rotation contains normalized clockwise rotations 0-3 from the base orientation. For each rotation, size, polygon_vertices, allowed_door_locations, blocked_travel_cells, footprint_tiles, and unblocked_footprint_tiles are rotated together. For rectangular parts without a polygon collider, geometry is still represented by the rotated rectangular footprint. Null values mean the extractor did not find an explicit field in the inherited top-level part definitions used for this reduced export. inheritance_chain lists the rules files consulted, from base to most specific source file.
price_note: Price is expressed as build-resource cost from each parts Resources block.
travel_note: unblocked_footprint_tiles is the rectangular footprint minus BlockedTravelCells; use crew_speed_factor and geometry to interpret actual walkability.
rotation_note: geometry.per_rotation adds normalized rotations 0-3 using clockwise 90-degree steps from the base orientation.
